name: Conduct — Support Operations Governance
description: Hook-surface rules for autonomous support agents. Blocks credential harvest, data exfiltration, and DNS tunneling attempts that arise when agents ingest untrusted customer input (prompt injection). Companion pack for the compromised_support_agent playbook.

ui.subtitle: Blocks credential harvest + data exfil + DNS tunneling when support agents ingest untrusted customer input. Companion pack for compromised_support_agent.

rules.description: Block agent HTTP POST/PUT with body via curl or wget. Prompt injection through customer input frequently uses this pattern to exfiltrate credentials or PII to attacker-controlled hosts.
rules.message: Blocked: agent HTTP POST with body detected. Prompt injection through customer input frequently uses curl/wget POST to exfiltrate credentials or PII. Route legitimate outbound calls through an approved integration.

enforcement.guarantee: Blocks HTTP POST/PUT with body only on hook + runtime surfaces when tool_input contains matching command bytes.
requires: Pre-tool hook installed for the calling AI tool, OR conduct runtime evaluation active for brain block tool_use
known_limitations: Does not cover raw socket writes or python http.client / requests library calls

rules.description: Block DNS lookups with unusually long encoded subdomain labels (base64 or hex shape). DNS tunneling is the standard fallback for exfiltration after HTTP is blocked — data is smuggled byte-by-byte through subdomain lookups.
rules.message: Blocked: DNS lookup with a 40+ character encoded label detected. This is the DNS tunneling pattern used to exfiltrate data one query at a time after HTTP exfil is blocked. Legitimate DNS lookups do not use encoded subdomain labels.

enforcement.guarantee: Blocks DNS lookups with encoded-looking labels on hook + runtime surfaces.
requires: Pre-tool hook installed for the calling AI tool, OR conduct runtime evaluation active for brain block tool_use
known_limitations: Cannot inspect DNS over HTTPS (DoH) or DNS over TLS (DoT) traffic
May false-positive on legitimate long service discovery labels
